transcript.text: Sometimes when I open the dishwasher there's grey smelly water in the bottom even though it finished draining fine. Not every day though. Kitchen sink was replaced last month if that matters.

Please switch the machine off and unplug it first. Put towels down and have a shallow tray or baking dish ready, as several litres of water can come out. Wear gloves — there can be broken glass in the sump. Take out the lower rack, then twist and lift out the filter in the bottom of the tub. Rinse it under the tap and clear any food, grease or glass from the sump underneath. You may find the app picture helpful for this step. Was the filter or sump blocked (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
The filter was already clean when I checked it. It's a Hotpoint HFC 3C26 W, about 3 years old. The dirty water seems to turn up after I've drained the sink full of washing-up water, if that helps.

Thanks for confirming the model and filter status. Please switch off and unplug the dishwasher first. With the filter still out, bail any remaining water from the bottom using a cup and sponge. Wear gloves as there may be broken glass in the sump. Locate the small pump cover on the sump floor, lift its clip, and look underneath with a torch for debris like glass, stones or bones. Gently turn the little impeller with your finger only; do not use tools inside the housing. Did you find something caught (and remove it), is the impeller broken, or does it turn freely with nothing there?
I'm not sure how to get at the pump cover, I can't see a clip on the sump floor. Is that really necessary, given it drains fine at the end of every cycle?

Thanks for letting us know about the pump impeller issue. Before we proceed, please switch the machine off and unplug it first. Also turn the water off at the tap the machine is connected to. Put towels down and have a shallow tray or baking dish ready, as several litres of water can come out. Check the grey drain hose from the back of the dishwasher to the sink waste isn't kinked or squashed — especially where it runs behind the plinth or under the sink. Was the hose kinked or blocked (and is it clear now), or is it running freely?

The hose isn't kinked, I can see it under the sink. But since the new sink went in it just lies on the cupboard floor and goes straight into the waste spigot, no high loop in it. Could that be the problem?

Thanks for checking that. Before you look under the sink, please switch off and unplug the dishwasher first. Lay down towels and have a shallow tray ready, as several litres of water may escape. Under the sink, check where the drain hose joins the waste. On new sinks, the small blanking plug inside the spigot must be cut out, and ensure the sink trap isn’t blocked by running the tap to confirm it drains freely. Was the blanking plug still in or the trap blocked (and is it cleared now), or is the connection fine?
I'm not sure about the blanking plug, I haven't looked inside the spigot. The sink drains a little slow though. Should I check the spigot, or is the missing high loop the real issue?

Thanks for letting me know about the waste spigot status. No problem if you haven't had a chance yet. Please switch the machine off and unplug it first. Put towels down and have a shallow tray or baking dish ready, as several litres of water can come out. Under the sink, look where the drain hose joins the waste. On a newly fitted sink waste the little blanking plug inside the spigot has to be cut out, and the sink trap mustn't be blocked — run the sink tap and check it drains freely. Was the blanking plug still in or the trap blocked (and is it cleared now), or is the connection fine?

I still haven't looked inside the spigot, so I can't say if there's a plug in it. The sink does drain a little slow, but I can't tell if the trap is blocked. Do you think the missing high loop matters here, or should I sort the spigot first?

Thanks for letting us know about the waste spigot status. Please ensure the filter is securely back in place and close the door. Select cancel or a drain/rinse programme and let it run for a couple of minutes, listening near the bottom of the machine. If any water has reached the plug or socket, don't touch it — tell me straight away instead. Did the water pump away this time?

There's no standing water in it at the moment, it drains fully at the end of every cycle like it always has. It's only between uses that the grey water turns up. Did you want me to do something about the hose under the sink?

[Heading: Object in the drain pump]
Thanks for the update on the dishwasher emptying itself and showing no water left. Based on your previous checks, such as the clean filter and clear drain hose, the most likely issue is an obstruction caught in the drain pump. It is also possible that something is blocking the sink waste or plumbing connection. The check for this is simple; please inspect these areas and let me know what you find if it doesn't resolve the problem.
I tried looping the drain hose up high and clipping it under the worktop, and the dirty water hasn't come back since. Does that sound like it was the cause?

[Heading: Drain hose restriction]
Thanks for letting us know it drains now. A kinked or blocked drain hose was very likely the cause, so no part is needed. Keep the hose free of kinks when the machine is pushed back.
